messages:
Maya: Heads up — we're seeing a p95 spike on hosted /v1/generate starting ~11:20UTC, p95 up from 130ms -> 820ms, p99 ~2.3s. Queue depth climbed to 60 on the api-runtime pool. :eyes:
Tom: Looking at graphs. Any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: deploy completed by sarah at 11:18UTC — release/optimize-batching (rev d2b7f3)
Luca: I see kernel-selector churn in the last 2m — many sessions switching between aux-xla and aux-cuda. Kernel select rate shot up 5x.
Maya: Also noticing KV cache eviction rate spiked, miss rate from 4%->28%. Might be a hotshard.
Tom: Can you paste the top counters? Luca, do we have a profiling snapshot?
Luca: quick counters:
```
timestamp: 2026-03-18T11:20:30Z
api_pool.queue_depth: 62
kernel_switch/sec: 480
kv_evictions/sec: 1200
batch_avg_size: 2.1 -> 1.3
latency.p95: 820ms
``` 
Luca: Profiling heap shows frequent small batches causing kernel jitter and falling back to generic kernels.
Sarah: The release included a sampler tweak that lowers coalescer window for tiny tokens — might be the batching heuristic change.
Rebecca: Also saw a tenant hammering embeddings endpoint around same time (spike in concurrent sessions 700->2700). Could be noisy neighbor.
OpsBot: Applied temporary rate cap on embeddings tenant T-392 at 11:24UTC.
Tom: After rate cap, queue depth dropped to ~18, p95 fell to ~190ms. Looks correlated.
Maya: For immediate mitigation we rolled back sampler tweak and pinned kernel affinity to primary-cuda on the pool. :thumbsup:
Sarah: Rolling back commit d2b7f3 in progress.
Luca: Follow-up tasks: (1) add a kernel-selector stability gate to reject excessive churn; (2) add KV hotshard detector alert; (3) revert batching window change more conservatively.
Maya: Can someone open a postmortem ticket and capture the exact timeline + flame graphs? I'll export a few profiles and the KV histograms.
Rebecca: I'll own tenant rate isolation improvements and propose per-tenant soft quotas.
Tom: Good. Tentatively no customer impact after 11:32UTC. We'll run longer heat test.
Sarah: Thanks all. Filing postmortem and scheduling a longer rollback verification.
Maya: TL;DR — root cause appears to be sampler heuristic change reducing coalescing, which reduced batch sizes and caused kernel selector oscillation + KV cache pressure; noisy tenant amplified queue build. Mitigation: rate cap + rollback + kernel pin. :white_check_mark:
